patterns: how many minutes in an hour
is an hour exactly a quarter day
entries.answer: An hour is sixty minutes and a quarter of a day, and it is the largest unit that divides a day evenly, which is why calendars and clocks are built around it. The word is also used loosely for any period at all, as in I will be there for an hour meaning approximately that long. Historically an hour was divided locally into sixty minutes, so what a minute meant depended on where you stood, and that is why astronomical time became the standard.

patterns: how many seconds in a minute
difference between minute detail and a minute late
entries.answer: A minute is sixty seconds and a sixtieth of an hour, and it is the unit people actually estimate with when judging whether something will take long. The word is also an adjective, as in a minute hand, a minute detail and a minute is not small. That double use for both a unit of time and something tiny is a real ambiguity, so I will be a minute late and that is a minute detail are not the same claim at all.

patterns: is a second a unit of time
entries.answer: A second is the base unit of time and also an ordinal, as in the second attempt, and the two senses rarely collide but do occasionally. As a unit it is a sixtieth of a minute, and an arc-second is a further sixtieth of that in the sky, so the subdivision runs all the way through astronomy. The informal use, meaning a very short while, is far more common in speech than the precise one, and English is comfortable with both.

entries.answer: A deadline is a time by which something must be finished, and the word quietly assumes the time was set from outside. That is the whole difference from a target, because a target can move and a deadline that moves has stopped being one. Deadlines earn their keep by concentrating effort, and the concentration is the entire benefit, since without a fixed finish people spread the work evenly across an unlimited span and complete none of it.

entries.answer: A schedule is a plan listing when things are meant to happen, and it differs from a timetable by being a plan rather than a published list. A timetable is fixed and external, as for trains, while a schedule is something a person or team arranges and changes. This is why a doctor has a schedule and a station has a timetable, and why rescheduling is an ordinary verb while retimetabling is not one.

entries.answer: Duration is the length of time something takes, and the word matters in law and in planning, where the same activity lasts a different amount depending on who is measuring. A task has a duration, a person has a lifespan and a subscription has a term, and English keeps those apart on purpose. Saying how long something lasts describes the thing itself, while saying how long it took describes the waiting, and the two can differ sharply.
